newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares tumble,C&C leads plunge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares tumble,C&C leads plunge.

text.p: Singapore shares plunged at midday on Friday after the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) broke key psychological support of 1,980 points and hit a 45-month low, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT, the STII lost 20.97 points or 1.05 percent to 1,968.83, the lowest level seen since August 1993.

"It's dragged down by Cycle & Carriage," a dealer said. She added investors were concerned C&C's motor division might be affected by keen competition from rival BMW and its property earnings dampened by weaker prices. Cycle & Carriage fell Singapore 50 cents to S$14.40 on volume of 74,000 shares.

Dealers said uncertainty over Wall Street and the lack of positive economic data from Singapore continued to pressure prices: "We had expected funds to stream in, but this is not the case," another dealer said.
Total market volume was around 107.7 million shares with 75 gainers to 182 losers.

Debutante Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin TIAN.SI was well-received and dominated trade, with over 55.5 million shares. It was trading at US$0.995 against its initial public offer price of US$0.68.
"The timing of its IPO is good because of the China-play. Fundamentally, it looks like a good stock," one analyst said.
Infrastructure firm Van der Horst took a breather from recent gains and eased four cents to S$2.66 on over 4.5 million shares.

"I think some people are getting nervous and want to see if the three key shareholders would buy back their stocks," one dealer said. He added there was also concern the forced sale of the company shares were larger than indicated.
Banks had to sell Van der Horst shares, pledged as collateral by its shareholders -- Johannes Kotjo, Johnlin Yuwono and Bambang Trihatmodjo -- last week when they failed to meet margin calls.
